column3: Close to the Greek; “save” is rendered “heal.”
NKJV includes “who had been sick,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “found the servant in good health.”
NKJV includes “many” with “His disciples,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
Close to the Greek; “bier” is rendered “open coffin.”
NKJV ends this verse after “all these things”; the critical text places “John, calling two of his disciples” at the end of verse 18, while NKJV puts it in verse 19.
NKJV begins with “And John, calling two of his disciples,” which the critical text places in verse 18. NKJV has “to Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “to the Lord.”
Close to the Greek; “palaces” is rendered “kings' courts.”
NKJV has “a greater prophet than John the Baptist,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “none is greater than John.”
Close to the Greek; “counsel” is rendered “will.”
